card_text: How Greater Noida installers can split campaigns between plotted-sector homes and Greater Noida West societies, handle single-point connections and book more site surveys.
intro:
Solar installer marketing in Greater Noida is really two jobs that look like one. On one side are the plotted sectors with Greek-letter names, Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Chi, Phi, Omicron and the rest, where an owner with a flat roof can decide on rooftop solar in a week. On the other side is Greater Noida West, the dense belt of high-rise societies along the Noida Extension stretch, where most residents can't install anything on their own and the real buyer is the society's apartment owners' association.

If one campaign tries to talk to both, you pay for flat owners who can't buy and miss the committees that can. This guide shows Greater Noida installers how to split the market, what to check on every lead, which channels suit each buyer, and how to turn enquiries into booked roof surveys. It builds on what we see across the 30+ solar EPCs and manufacturers we work with.

sections.h2: Two Greater Noidas: know which buyer you're paying for
sections.html:
Before you write an ad, decide which of these buyers each campaign is for:

BuyerWhereWho decidesWhat they ask first
Plot and independent house ownersPlotted residential sectors such as Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Chi, Phi, Omicron and Swarn Nagri; older villages being rebuilt as independent floorsThe owner, often with family members who live on other floorsTotal cost after subsidy, how many kW the roof can take, how long the bill savings take
Societies and AOAsGreater Noida West high-rises and the group housing pockets near Pari Chowk and along the expresswaysAOA or RWA committee, then a general body voteCommon-area bill savings, roof waterproofing, who maintains the plant, subsidy paperwork
Commercial and institutionalEcotech industrial sectors, Udyog Vihar, Surajpur and Kasna sites, Knowledge Park colleges and schoolsOwner, plant head or finance teamPayback, capex vs RESCO, installation downtime

Most installers do best by running the house-owner campaign every month and treating societies and factories as a separate sales project with its own budget. This post focuses on the first two; our solar marketing agency page covers how we run commercial pipelines.

sections.h2: Greater Noida facts to get right in ads and on calls
sections.html:
Greater Noida buyers compare notes with neighbours and read the fine print. A few facts shape every conversation:

  • The DISCOM. Most of Greater Noida is supplied by Noida Power Company Limited (NPCL), a private distribution company. Some pockets of Noida Extension and the surrounding villages may fall under Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam (PVVNL) instead. Don't guess: ask for a photo of the latest electricity bill, which shows the supplier, consumer number and sanctioned load.
  • Sanctioned load caps the system. Under UP's rooftop rules the plant generally can't exceed the sanctioned load on the connection. If a 2 kW connection wants a 5 kW plant, the owner needs a load enhancement first. Say this early so the quote doesn't fall apart at the net-metering stage.
  • Central subsidy. Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana the central subsidy for homes is ₹30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and ₹18,000 for the third kW, capped at ₹78,000. For societies, central assistance of ₹18,000 per kW is available for common facilities, for plants up to 500 kW.
  • State top-up. Uttar Pradesh has offered an additional state subsidy for residential rooftop solar through UPNEDA on top of the central amount. The amount and conditions have changed over time, so check UPNEDA's current rules before you put a number in an ad.
  • Single-point connections. Many Greater Noida West societies take one bulk connection and bill flats through sub-meters. A flat owner in such a society usually can't apply for their own net meter, which is another reason flat-owner leads rarely convert.

Write subsidy claims carefully. Our guide to using PM Surya Ghar in ads shows wording that stays accurate when the rules move.

sections.h2: Solar installer marketing in Greater Noida's plotted sectors
sections.html:
Plot owners are the fastest buyers in the city, and the easiest to target precisely:

  1. Target by sector, not by city. On Meta, use a radius or pin list around the plotted sectors you can reach in a day, and exclude the high-rise clusters if your form isn't built for them. On Google, build ad groups around searches such as "solar panel installation in Greater Noida", "solar company Greater Noida" and sector-plus-solar searches, and add negatives for jobs, training, franchise and dealership searches.
  2. Ask house-type questions in the form. "Do you own the roof?", "Independent house, builder floor or society flat?", "Average monthly bill?" and "Which sector?" cut most of the wasted calls.
  3. Handle the builder-floor question. Where a plot has been rebuilt as three or four floors with different owners, the roof often belongs to the top-floor owner or is shared. Your sales script should ask who has roof rights before you send a surveyor.
  4. Show local proof. Photos of plants on Greater Noida rooftops, with the sector named, do more than stock images. Ask every finished customer for a Google review that mentions the area.

Our Noida rooftop solar leads guide has a longer list of qualifying questions you can adapt.

Society solar is a slower sale with a much bigger order, and the market is warming up. In July 2026 the Arihant Arden apartment owners' association in Greater Noida West commissioned a 500 kWp rooftop plant under PM Surya Ghar, reported as the district's first high-rise society project under the scheme, and news reports named other societies in the pipeline. Committees in nearby societies notice projects like that.

To reach them:

  1. Make a short list of societies with large terrace areas and high common-area bills (lifts, pumps, corridor and parking lighting).
  2. Approach the committee, not residents. Ask for a slot at the next AOA meeting. Bring a one-page summary: estimated common-area savings, subsidy process, roof waterproofing plan and maintenance terms.
  3. Give residents something to read. A plain-language FAQ for WhatsApp groups helps the committee win the general body vote.
  4. Use ads only for awareness. A small Meta campaign shown to residents of a society you're already pitching, with a video of a society plant elsewhere, keeps your name in front of voters. Don't expect it to generate direct leads.

Plan for weeks or months of follow-up per society, and track each one as a deal, not as a lead.

sections.h2: From enquiry to booked roof survey
sections.html:
Many installers lose more money after the lead arrives than before it. A simple routine helps:

  1. Call within 10 minutes during working hours. If there's no answer, send a WhatsApp message with your name, company and a request for the latest electricity bill.
  2. From the bill, confirm the DISCOM, sanctioned load and monthly usage before you quote a size.
  3. Confirm ownership and roof rights, especially for builder floors.
  4. Offer two survey slots, not "when are you free?".
  5. After the survey, send a written quote that shows gross price, the subsidy you expect them to claim, net cost and the net-metering steps.

Log every lead with its source, sector, house type, survey booked and installed. After a month you'll know which sectors and channels give you installations, not just enquiries. At scale, our solar clients typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week; your numbers will depend on your budget, area and follow-up. Our rooftop campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when they're working well, but judge each channel by cost per survey and per installation.

faqs: Which electricity company serves Greater Noida for solar net metering?

Most of Greater Noida is supplied by Noida Power Company Limited (NPCL). Some pockets of Noida Extension and nearby villages may be under PVVNL. The customer's latest electricity bill shows the supplier, consumer number and sanctioned load, so ask for it before you quote.
Can a flat owner in a Greater Noida West society install rooftop solar?

Usually not individually. The roof is common property and many societies use a single-point bulk connection, so solar is normally installed by the AOA or RWA for common areas. Installers should pitch the committee rather than individual flat owners.
How much subsidy can Greater Noida homeowners get for rooftop solar?

Under PM Surya Ghar the central subsidy is ₹30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and ₹18,000 for the third kW, up to ₹78,000. Uttar Pradesh has also offered a state top-up through UPNEDA. Check the current amounts on the official portals before you advertise a figure.
What is the best way to get solar leads in Greater Noida?

Run Meta lead ads and Google Search ads targeted at the plotted sectors you serve, with ownership and house-type questions in the form, keep your Google Business Profile active with local reviews, and treat societies as a separate committee-led sales process.
